ground_truth.description: Changed loop from '0..n' to '0..=n' (inclusive range). This iterates n+1 times instead of n, creating n+2 vertices instead of the documented n+1. On the last iteration (i=n), params[i] will panic with index-out-of-bounds since params has length n (indices 0..n-1). Even if it didn't panic, the simplex would have the wrong dimensionality for Nelder-Mead.
With the inclusive range 0..=n, when i=n the expression 'params[i]' accesses index n in a slice of length n, causing a panic. The original 0..n range correctly limited i to 0..n-1.
validate_simplex() is defined but never called. If it were used to validate the output of build_simplex, it would catch the off-by-one bug at runtime.

task.title: Make the Nelder-Mead initial simplex step scale configurable
task.description: `build_simplex` in `crates/reify-constraints/src/solver.rs` hard-codes the initial perturbation at 10% of each parameter's effective range, which is too coarse for tightly-bounded problems and too fine for wide ones, and the solve path has no way to pick a different step. Thread the step fraction through as a `scale: f64` argument and use it in place of the literal `0.1`, preserving the documented simplex shape: the initial point plus exactly one perturbation per dimension, each perturbation offset along its own dimension and clamped into that parameter's effective bounds. Add a `validate_simplex(simplex: &[Vec<f64>], n: usize) -> bool` predicate that checks a built simplex has the vertex count and per-vertex dimensionality Nelder-Mead requires, so the solve path and tests can reject a malformed simplex before it reaches the optimizer. Observable outcome: callers choose the step fraction per problem and the simplex shape is checkable at the boundary.
task.test_strategy: Unit-test `build_simplex` for 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional inputs at two different `scale` values: assert `validate_simplex` accepts each result, that vertex `i + 1` differs from the initial point only in dimension `i` and by `(hi - lo) * scale` before clamping, and that a perturbation landing outside the bounds is clamped. Add negative cases for `validate_simplex` (wrong vertex count, short vertex) and confirm the existing solver convergence tests still pass with the default scale. `cargo test -p reify-constraints`.
